nodes.bodyText: PR author is not in the allowed authors list.

Thanks a lot for this — and especially for the honest scoping section. You're right that the deployed router serves frontend/out as static assets via registerUIStatic, so the server-side Next advisories aren't reachable in prod; calling that out yourself instead of leading with "8 CVEs, merge now" is genuinely appreciated and makes triage easier.
This one follows the repo's conventions, so no changes needed from my side. Verified locally on your head commit:

npm ci in frontend/ installs cleanly from the committed lockfile — no EOVERRIDE/EUSAGE, so the postcss devDependency/override lockstep bump is correct.
npm install --package-lock-only produces zero lockfile churn (identical SHA-256), i.e. the committed lockfile is exactly what npm would generate.
npm run build passes — static export completes, all 8 pages prerendered and exported.
Lockfile diff is narrowly scoped to next, its @next/swc-* platform binaries, eslint-config-next + @next/eslint-plugin-next, postcss (+ transitive nanoid), and js-yaml. All 502 resolved tarballs still point at registry.npmjs.org, no Git/HTTP resolutions and no new install scripts.
Nothing outside frontend/package.json + frontend/package-lock.json, so none of the Go-side rules in the root AGENTS.md (layer/import model, no magic strings for provider or model names, sentinel errors, slog, minimal comments, non-tautological tests) are engaged here — a manifest-only patch bump within the same minor line is exactly the low-risk shape we want for these.

Two non-blocking notes, purely FYI:

The lockfile resolves postcss to 8.5.25 and js-yaml to 4.3.1, both published within the last week. The fixed floors you cite (8.5.18, 4.3.0) are what the advisories require, so pinning the resolutions closer to those floors is slightly more conservative against a freshly-published-version supply-chain risk. Not worth another round trip here — the ranges are right either way.
frontend has no ESLint config, so npm run lint (next lint) drops into an interactive setup wizard. Pre-existing and unrelated to your change — just flagging so it doesn't surprise you if you touch the frontend again.

Happy to take the brace-expansion npm update as a separate follow-up PR if you'd like to file it; keeping it out of this diff was the right call. Also, for context: the greptile-apps[bot] "PR author is not in the allowed authors list" comment is just our bot's author allowlist, not review feedback on your work.

nodes.bodyText:
Someone is attempting to deploy a commit to the World Monitor Team on Vercel.
A member of the Team first needs to authorize it.

Greptile Summary
This PR raises the desktop shell's Tauri dependency floor to the first release containing the origin-confusion fix.

Restricts the runtime dependency to Tauri versions from 2.11.1 up to, but excluding, 3.0.
Leaves the checked-in Cargo lockfile unchanged.

Confidence Score: 4/5
The dependency constraint is safe to merge, but the lockfile should be regenerated and committed to preserve deterministic desktop builds.
The patched Tauri floor is correctly declared, while the stale 2.10.3 lock entry forces unlocked builds to re-resolve dependencies and causes locked builds to reject the dependency state.
src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/Cargo.lock
Important Files Changed



Filename
Overview




src-tauri/Cargo.toml
Correctly raises the Tauri security floor, but the committed Cargo.lock remains inconsistent with the new requirement.




Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: "fix(security): require tauri >=2.11.1 to..." | Re-trigger Greptile

Revalidated against current head per #5902's rule that an open PR is not automatically the correct fix — and this one turned out not to be landable as written, through no fault of the analysis: the write-up here is accurate and the constraint you chose is the right one.
The gap is that the change is Cargo.toml-only. Cargo.lock still pins the vulnerable 2.10.3, and the lockfile is what decides what ships. Reproduced on a branch from current main with just this change applied:
$ cargo metadata --locked
error: the lock file .../Cargo.lock needs to be updated but --locked was passed

So merging this alone would have failed every --locked build — the desktop-rust PR gate added in #5915, and the release build — while still shipping 2.10.3. Exactly the "To complete the fix" step your description calls out, which turns out to be load-bearing rather than a follow-up.
#5934 completes it: your manifest constraint verbatim, plus the regenerated lockfile (tauri 2.11.5, the latest patched 2.x, with its runtime family — tauri-build 2.6.3, tauri-runtime 2.11.3, tauri-runtime-wry 2.11.4, tauri-utils 2.9.3, wry 0.55.1, tao 0.35.3). An unpinned cargo update -p tauri was rejected for dragging unrelated transitive churn (cssparser, html5ever, derive_more) into a security patch.
It also adds scripts/check-rust-security-floors.mjs, because your report exposed that nothing in CI inspects Cargo.lock at all — security-audit covers npm lockfiles only — so a later cargo update could have silently undone this with zero signal. The floor now runs in the PR gate and in the release workflow.
Verified: cargo test --locked 14/14 on 2.11.5, including the require_trusted_window IPC tests you correctly identified as the partial mitigation. Your analysis of the exploitability here was spot on.
Closing in favour of #5934 — credited there. Thanks for the careful report.

nodes.title: fix(deps): patch ajv/ws/protobufjs/vite for disclosed CVEs

nodes.bodyText:
Thanks @KnockOutEZ — both addressed in 21b6922:

Lockfile regenerated (npm install --package-lock-only). ajv now resolves to 8.20.0, deduping cleanly with the openapi-validator's 8.20.0 as you noted, so npm ci should pass.
protobufjs override bounded to ">=7.6.1 <8" — now resolves to 7.6.5 (was jumping to 8.7.1). Left ws/vite in-major as you flagged.

Ready for CI whenever you approve the run.

Thanks for bounding the range and regenerating the lockfile — that fixed the npm ci failure. But CI now trips a different, more fundamental guard, and I owe you a correction on my earlier advice.
tests/unit/package-deps.test.ts fails: overrides.protobufjs is absent. That test is a deliberate regression guard for #114 / #101, and the reason is important here: npm only honors an overrides block from the install root. When wigolo is installed as a dependency — which is exactly what npx wigolo and every MCP client does — npm ignores wigolo's own overrides. So the ws / protobufjs / vite overrides in this PR don't actually reach shipped users; they only affect this repo's local dev tree. We learned this the hard way when an earlier overrides-based fix (#101) left end users still hitting the bug (#114).
So the override strategy can't close these transitive CVEs for real. Suggested path:

Keep the ajv bump — it's a direct dependency, so bumping it in dependencies genuinely propagates. That part is good and worth keeping on its own.
Drop the ws / protobufjs / vite overrides. For the transitive ones (ws, protobufjs), the only fix that reaches npx consumers is bumping the parent dependency that pulls them once it releases a patched version — same situation you already documented for tar/fastembed. vite is a devDependency (build-time only, never shipped), so its advisory doesn't reach end users at runtime.

Net: I'd narrow this PR to just the ajv bump (real, shippable), and track ws/protobufjs as upstream-parent-bump follow-ups alongside tar. Sorry for the earlier steer toward bounding the range — I should have caught the overrides-don't-propagate issue first.

Thanks for the correction — and no need to apologise, that's a genuinely non-obvious npm behaviour and you caught it before it shipped as a false fix.
Narrowed to just the ajv bump in f731378. Dropped the ws / protobufjs / vite overrides.
You're right on the mechanism, and it's worse than "the overrides don't help" — they were also redundant here. I removed all three and re-resolved the tree from scratch with no overrides block at all:



package
resolves to (no overrides)
patched?

8.21.1
yes

yes


vite
8.1.5
yes



So in this repo's own tree the parents already admit patched versions, and the overrides were pinning what npm would have picked anyway — while doing nothing for npx consumers, exactly as you said. Belt with no trousers.
package-lock.json is unchanged: it already records no overrides, and npm ci is consistent against it. The package-deps guard now passes, including overrides.protobufjs is absent.
Tracking ws and protobufjs as upstream-parent-bump follow-ups alongside tar/fastembed — agreed that bumping the parent once it releases a patched version is the only thing that actually reaches end users. I'll open those separately rather than widening this PR again.
ajv stays at ^8.18.0, resolving to 8.20.0 and deduping with the openapi-validator as you noted.

nodes.title: fix(deps): bump brace-expansion to ^5.0.8 (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, HIGH)

nodes.bodyText:
🔍 OpenCodeReview found 1 issue(s) in this PR.

✅ Successfully posted inline: 1 comment(s)

Closing this — you've fixed it properly in #561 (ea50569), and your approach is better than this PR's.
Bumping minimatch to 10.2.6 so brace-expansion@5.x comes in as a natural transitive, bounded to >=5.0.8 <6, closes GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg at the source. This PR instead forced brace-expansion to ^5.0.8 underneath minimatch@^9.0.7 via resolutions, which is the blunter instrument.
One data point that may be worth keeping, since it validates the route you took: forcing v5 under the old chain broke the lint toolchain. CI here failed with
TypeError: (0 , brace_expansion_1.default) is not a function
    at node_modules/@eslint/eslintrc/dist/eslintrc.cjs:1097:16

@eslint/eslintrc (via ESLint 8.57.1) does a CJS require() and calls the default export as a function. brace-expansion@2.x was plain CJS with module.exports = expand; 5.x ships dual ESM/CJS via exports, so the interop default lands differently and the call fails. So the override alone wasn't viable regardless of the advisory — the surrounding chain had to move too, which is exactly what #561 does.
For the record on the bot review above: it flagged that minimatch@^9.0.7 needs brace-expansion@2.x. That wasn't right — minimatch@9.0.7 declares brace-expansion: ^5.0.2, so the pre-existing >=2.1.2 <3 pin was itself the inconsistent one. The real incompatibility was @eslint/eslintrc, not minimatch.
No action needed from you. Thanks for the quick turnaround on the advisory.

Filed by Aeon.

Closing as superseded by #561 (ea50569, merged today), which patches the same brace-expansion DoS by bumping minimatch to 10.2.6. That reaches the vulnerable transitive dep through the parent, which is the durable fix; a direct ^5.0.8 override here would only have covered this repo's own tree and conflicted with @eslint/eslintrc's CJS require of brace-expansion's dual export. Closing this as superseded — you already fixed it, and you fixed it better than this PR did.
c1f5f81 ("fix: remediate vanta dependency advisories", 2026-07-20) bumped both packages on main:

multer ^2.0.2 → ^2.2.0 (identical to what this PR proposed)
nodemailer ^8.0.2 → ^9.0.3

The nodemailer jump to 9.x matters. This PR targeted the 8.x line, and 8.x never fixes GHSA-p6gq-j5cr-w38f (HIGH, message-level raw option bypasses disableFileAccess / disableUrlAccess) — that one is only fixed in 9.0.1. So the 8.x route I proposed would have closed three of the four advisories and quietly left the fourth open. Your 9.0.3 closes all four. OSV reports zero known advisories for nodemailer@9.0.3 and multer@2.2.0 as of today.
That also makes this branch actively harmful to merge now: it conflicts with main, and resolving it in this PR's favour would downgrade nodemailer from ^9.0.3 back to ^8.0.11.
@Fermionic-Lyu — on your review point, you were right, and it was worth more than it looked. backend/package.json declared ^8.0.9 while the lockfile resolved 8.0.11. I pushed a commit aligning them before spotting that main had already moved past all of it. Nothing further needed here.
Thanks for the review time, and apologies for the noise on an issue you'd already handled.
